sentences.text: Dalianraptor resembled the avialian Jeholornis but featured a longer thumb and shorter forelimbs, suggesting it may have been flightless.
This creature reached a total length of about 80 cm.
The holotype specimen D2139 was discovered before the 2000s and was initially labeled as a possible dromaeosaurid.
Dalianraptor is classified within the parent group Avialae.
It is also classified under the class Reptilia.
Dalianraptor lived in China approximately 120 million years ago during the early Cretaceous period.
Fossils of Dalianraptor were found in the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning province.
The animal lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
Researchers suspect the holotype might be a fossil trade chimera consisting of a Jeholornis body with arms from a flightless theropod.
